To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there are six types of achievement strategies that can be identified in an unselected population of adolescents.
the adolescents in the mastery-oriented group reported the highest levels of well-being and achievement.

adolescents who use functional strategies, such as mastery-oriented and defensive strategies, are more successful and well adjusted than are adolescents who use dysfunctional strategies, such as self-handicapping, learned helplessness and defensive strategies, and that the use of functional strategies is positively associated with well-being and school adjustment and negatively associated with norm-breaking behaviour, whereas the use of dysfunctional strategies is negatively associated with well-being.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the types of strategies adolescents deploy, the correlates of these strategies and how these strategies are related to well-being and school adjustment.
the identification of the types of strategies adolescents use in achievement context and the relationship between these strategies and well-being, school achievement and norm-breaking behaviour.
the development of a new instrument, the Achievement Strategies Questionnaire (ASQ), which is a self-report instrument for assessing achievement strategies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the deployment of functional strategies is related to positive adjustment and the deployment of dysfunctional strategies is related to negative adjustment.
adolescents with the functional strategies were better off in terms of well-being and achievement than those with the dysfunctional strategies.
the deployment of functional strategies is associated with positive outcomes in school.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the strategies that adolescents deploy in achievement contexts are important for their well-being, their school adjustment and for their school achievement.
achievement strategies are important for the development of well-being in adolescents.
the adolescents who are more successful in school are those who are able to deploy strategies that are more functional, such as optimistic and defensive-pessimistic strategies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are different types of achievement strategies, which can be classified in terms of their function, and that the function of a strategy can be predicted by the way the strategy is defined.
there is no single strategy that works best for everyone.
the strategies adolescents use are related to well-being and school adjustment.
